FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

2. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.

3. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

4. When practising Reading for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Vocabulary.

5. When practising Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression.

6. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

7. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.

8. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. fenêtre
   B. livre
   C. chaise
   D. porte

9. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good morning / hello
   B. Good night only
   C. Excuse me
   D. Thank you

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Informative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Vocabulary.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

8. B — livre

9. A — Good morning / hello
